transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Victor Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jane Miller (Southridge), Carlos Reyes (Southridge), Imani Okafor (Southridge)

Summary:
High-level compliance intake: Southridge is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for inference. Primary constraints: strict EU residency for EU customers, SOC2 + internal audit evidence, 7-year financial logs retention, key material residency and HSM requirements for certain regulated products. They want to validate that Redwood can provide region-lock, keystore routing, redaction pipelines for logs, and a minimal evidence bundle for auditors. Also discuss performance tradeoffs (latency/cost) and an initial pilot on Dedicated.

Topics covered:
- Deployment models (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and where logs/audit live
- Keystore/KMS residence & HSM/escrow options
- Log retention / redaction / segmentation for financial records
- Evidence for SOC 2 / ISO / regulator audits
- Pilot plan and timeline

Action items (captured): see action_items field

Transcript body:
00:00 Victor Chen: okay folks, morning / afternoon depending where you are, thanks for taking the time. this is Victor on the AE side, Priya our solutions engineer is here. quick roll call?
00:08 Jane Miller: hi jane here, head of data governance at Southridge.
00:10 Carlos Reyes: carlos, cloud architect.
00:12 Imani Okafor: imani, compliance.
00:14 Priya Nair: priya, se at Redwood. thanks all. 
00:22 Victor Chen: great. objective today per the invite was to understand residency and evidence needs and scope an initial pilot. quick high level: are we looking at hosting for production or just evaluating pilot first?
00:36 Jane Miller: pilot first. we want to prototype with a small user subset in eu and us regions. long term we'll need region-locked processing for eu pII and financial data. we are evaluating whether dedicated capacity in redwood, or a private deployment in our vpc makes more sense. obviously cost and ops are considerations.
00:56 Victor Chen: got it. when you say region-locked processing, you mean both inference compute + logs must stay in region? or logs can be centralized?
01:08 Jane Miller: for eu customers, compute and logs need to remain in the eu. some internal services can centralize, but regulators ask for evidence that eu data never left eu. logs that contain pII have to be redacted or kept in eu.
01:24 Imani Okafor: yes and for our audit trail we need tamper-evident audit logs accessible to us. retention requirement is... we have a 7 year minimum for financial transaction metadata per our legal team.
01:36 Priya Nair: okay. we can do region locking with both dedicated and private. Hosted (multi-tenant) we typically provision region-specific endpoints but need to map controls. with Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools in the region and logs can be pushed to your customer-owned SIEM via secure forwarding. Private offers the most control (VPC or on-prem).
01:54 Carlos Reyes: for keystores, we need the keys to be managed in our HSM or KMS—no cross-border key replication. how does redwood do KMS?
02:06 Priya Nair: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via KMS integrations. you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and we support HSM-backed keys in supported clouds. for Private on-prem, the keystore can be customer-run; for Dedicated we also do KMS integration with region scope. I'll add a diagram after the call.
02:20 Victor Chen: quick question: does Redwood store payloads in logs by default? i.e., are prompts or completions part of audit logs?
02:30 Priya Nair: by default we redact sensitive content in logs and we provide configurable redaction and sampling. there are modes where you can turn on full request/response logging for debugging but that's opt-in and typically used only during POCs with strict access controls.
02:44 Jane Miller: our legal insists on never storing raw prompts for eu accounts. can you guarantee that?
02:49 Priya Nair: we can't legally guarantee in a raw sense but we can, in Dedicated and Private, configure log pipelines so that prompt text is redacted before it leaves the region and is not persisted in control plane logs. for Hosted multi-tenant there are additional controls but if you need absolute separation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
03:12 Imani Okafor: what about immutable audit trails? auditors ask for tamper evidence and who accessed what. does Redwood provide S3-style object versioning and signed logs?
03:22 Priya Nair: we expose export hooks to push logs to your GCS/S3 bucket and you can enable object lock / WORM. we also offer signed access logs and API access events in the audit stream. I'll include examples in the evidence bundle.
03:36 Carlos Reyes: latency is a concern: if we push logs through a redaction pipeline that sits in the eu, does that add to inference latency?
03:46 Priya Nair: redaction runs asynchronously for most workflows. the inference path keeps token latency low; we do prefix caching and streaming. for synchronous logging that must be in-line that could add ms-level overhead; we typically recommend asynchronous ingest + immediate availability in a short window.
04:05 Victor Chen: can we talk about the regulator ask re: key escrow? they requested a mechanism to recover keys in an emergency but they want control.
04:15 Jane Miller: yes our counsel asked whether there's support for key escrow, or key rotation logs we can audit.
04:21 Priya Nair: Redwood supports rotation logs and KMS audit trails. for escrow, we can integrate with third-party escrow vendors or provide manual escrow workflows for Private installs. for Dedicated, we can support a split-control model where keys are held in customer KMS and we get wrapped keys for inference in region.
04:40 Imani Okafor: are you SOC2 type 2 and do you have ISO attestation? we need to list that in our procurement pack.
04:47 Victor Chen: yes we have SOC2 type 2 and ISO 27001 — i'll send the evidence pack after the call.
04:53 Jane Miller: good. also curious about data residency proof. our auditors expect demonstrable policies that show no egress. how is that shown?
05:05 Priya Nair: we can provide region logs, routing rules, and configuration snapshots that show geofences on the control plane. for Private deployments, the control plane can be customer-hosted so evidence is straightforward. for Dedicated we provide routing configuration and network traces that auditors accept.
05:26 Carlos Reyes: any multi-tenant contamination risk? we need assurance on tenant isolation, both at the GPU process level and logs.
05:33 Priya Nair: isolation is a core design point. Dedicated gives you isolated pools with tenant mapping. multi-tenant Hosted shares model instances sometimes with vtable-level isolation; that said, for regulated data we steer customers to Dedicated or Private.
05:50 Victor Chen: what's the typical SLA for Dedicated?
05:54 Priya Nair: we offer SLA-backed latency percentiles and uptime for Dedicated customers, with an ops escalation flow and a runbook for failover. details in the annex of the quote.
06:06 Jane Miller: how do you handle legal hold/ e-discovery requests? we have to be able to put data under a hold and not delete even if retention policy would purge it.
06:18 Priya Nair: we support retention overrides and legal-hold markers. the data retention system is policy-driven and you can pin buckets with a hold flag. we'll show the controls in the demo.
06:29 Carlos Reyes: on the tech side — can we run an initial benchmark on a dedicated worker with our typical prompt mix? we want to measure 95th percentile token latency and token cost.
06:40 Victor Chen: absolutely, that's in scope for a POC. Priya, what do you need to set that up?
06:44 Priya Nair: ideally a small set of representative prompts, rates, and sequence lengths, plus which model variant you'd like us to run. we can provision a dedicated pool for a week for benchmarking. also need network ACL/IP allowlist so we can accept traffic from your test harness.
06:58 Jane Miller: we can provide prompts, but some are production prompts with real customer data; we'd like to synthetic-ize them. is synthetic data fine for benchmarking?
07:07 Priya Nair: yes, synthetic is fine, we only need distribution of tokens and typical sequences. for the EU pilot we can run everything in eu region to simulate residency.
07:18 Imani Okafor: on redaction, can we run pre-ingest redaction? we have patterns for account numbers and other identifiers that need to be scrubbed before logging or copying into any analytics pipeline.
07:30 Priya Nair: yes, we have pre-ingest webhook filters and regex-based redaction templates. we can also support custom ML-based scrubbers as an integration.
07:45 Carlos Reyes: about cost — private on-prem looks expensive but gives us the keystore control. Dedicated seems middle ground. do you have ballpark delta?
07:56 Victor Chen: yes there are tradeoffs. Private on-prem has a platform and support fee plus infra Opex. Dedicated is a committed capacity model — lower capex but monthly commit. Hosted is lowest onboarding friction but less isolation. priya will send a cost delta spreadsheet.
08:12 Priya Nair: i'll include typical CPU/GPU counts for throughput targets and a draft cost model.
08:20 Jane Miller: how do you handle cross-border failover? if an eu region goes down do we failover to us? that would violate residency requirements.
08:31 Priya Nair: our routing policies allow for region-specific fallbacks: you can choose strict region lock (no cross-border failover) or relaxed (fallback to secondary region). for regulated workloads we recommend strict. if you choose strict and region fails completely we can fail closed or queue requests until region recovers.
08:51 Imani Okafor: auditors also ask for identity management — SSO, SAML, SCIM, RBAC. what's available?
08:58 Priya Nair: SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, granular RBAC, token-level access logs; we integrate with enterprise IdP.
09:08 Carlos Reyes: are there any legal blockers for using third-party model weights? we use some in-house models, but we may need to mix with open models.
09:18 Priya Nair: you can bring your own model with Private, and Dedicated supports bringing model artifacts in many cases. for Hosted there's a curated model catalog. we'll map the model onboarding path once you share the artifact details.
09:31 Victor Chen: question from procurement: what is your standard data processing addendum and data transfer agreements for eu?
09:37 Priya Nair: we have a DPA that includes SCCs where necessary and region-specific data processing terms; legal can provide the template.
09:45 Jane Miller: ok, small but important: are system-generated prompts (like system messages or tool call traces) considered logs? we want to exclude some internal traces.
09:55 Priya Nair: they are logs unless redacted. you can annotate which message categories to suppress from logs.
10:05 Victor Chen: great. let's move to the pilot scope and timeline. what does success look like for you Jane?
10:12 Jane Miller: success is twofold: technical — demonstrate sub-100ms token latency on our common paths and no data egress from eu; compliance — provide an evidence bundle for auditors that shows region-locking, keystore residency, and retention controls.
10:28 Carlos Reyes: operational success is a clear runbook for incident escalation and how we roll back changes if something misroutes.
10:36 Priya Nair: we'll provide a runbook and playbook; we can do a joint run-through on day 1 of the pilot.
10:42 Imani Okafor: timeline — procurement would like to close pilot approvals by 2026-04-15. is that feasible?
10:49 Victor Chen: yes, if we move quickly on evidence and we get your in-scope list by next week.
10:55 Jane Miller: we'll try. also we'd like to see a sample of the audit logs we would get, redacted.
11:02 Priya Nair: we can share sanitized samples and also sample log schemas.
11:08 Carlos Reyes: ok, security question: for Dedicated can you guarantee no host-level console access from Redwood staff? we want to limit access for certain classes of systems during the pilot.
11:18 Priya Nair: we can gate access via IAM roles and temporary just-in-time access with justification. private on-prem gives you full control. Dedicated can be configured to minimize vendor access; there are standard support flows that require your approval for certain operations.
11:33 Jane Miller: last question from me: do you have any customers in EU financial services you can reference?
11:38 Victor Chen: yes, we have a couple of references in EMEA (redacted in this transcript) and we can provide an intro under NDA.
11:46 Imani Okafor: perfect. any blockers from Redwood side to start the pilot?
11:50 Priya Nair: we need the in-scope prompts, test harness IPs, and confirmation of which regions to test plus a PO or MSA signature for resource allocation.
11:59 Victor Chen: i'll follow up on the PO/contract process and attach the DPA and evidence zip.
12:04 Jane Miller: thanks all. this was helpful.

Closing recap (12:04):
- Victor: send SOC2/ISO evidence pack and DPA template; attach procurement contact.
- Priya: send architecture diagram for Dedicated vs Private, redaction patterns, sample sanitized logs, and cost delta spreadsheet; outline pilot provisioning requirements.
- Jane: provide list of in-scope systems and synthetic prompt set; confirm legal hold/retention windows.

End of call.
